trace.topic: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More.
trace.goal: Explain the paradox that AI agents increase managerial and operational work.
expected_facts: The answer should explain that AI agents expand what teams can attempt, which often increases work.
It should argue that management, supervision, and orchestration become more important, not less.
It should connect the paradox to founder expectations about leverage.
rubric_must_haves: Names and explains the paradox clearly.
Connects the idea to day-to-day operating reality.
Includes a concrete implication for founders or managers.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should explain that AI agents create leverage, but leverage usually expands the amount of work teams attempt rather than shrinking the need for judgment and management. As a result, founders often find themselves supervising more workflows, more experiments, and more exceptions. The lesson is to expect amplified operations, not effortless simplification.

trace.answer: So what’s your excuse now? If there really was no way to get something done before … how many excuses will we have after? We’re all still figuring this out, so I’m just sharing my learnings here. My first agent took me about 30 days to train and deploy. That was hard. And then another one took me maybe 15-20 days to train and deploy. Now my latest AI Agent took me roughly 24 hours to deploy! So I guess you could say I got a lot faster with each new deployment. But also — why would I take time off anymore? 😉
trace.raw_model_output: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More. What if the productivity gains from AI weren’t actually productivity gains? What if AI didn’t free up time for strategy sessions and golf games? What if instead, we just found ourselves working harder, faster, longer? That’s what’s happening right now with many companies deploying AI agents—employees aren’t getting more done because of AI. They’re doing more because AI makes them feel like they should be doing more. Here’s why this matters deeply: If your team isn’t seeing increased output and reduced stress after implementing AI agents, you haven’t failed. But you might have missed something important about how these tools really work—and why some people will use them to push themselves harder rather than easier. The Cognitive Load Illusion We all assumed AI would reduce cognitive load. And it does—for simple tasks. But when AI handles complex problems requiring deep thinking, judgment, and creativity, here’s what happens: The boundary between “work” and “not work” gets erased entirely. Every moment becomes potentially productive. Every pause feels wasteful. Your brain starts generating new ideas while you’re eating dinner. Your unconscious mind keeps processing during sleep. Your subconscious continues evaluating options during relaxation. When every second could theoretically contribute to success, motivation shifts from having time off to needing to stay engaged. This isn’t rational behavior. It’s psychological response to technological possibility. trace.retrieval_query: The Cowan Paradox: Why AI Agents Won’t Let You Do Less Work. They’ll Make You Do More.

retrieval_hits.text: Because AI, used right, enables you to do more things at scale than were ever possible before.

"20 AI Agents aren't less work than the humans they replaced.

But it's just ... easier.  They don't quit, they don't stop, they don't need promotions or even career growth.

It's easier to work with well-trained AI Agents than ... mid-pack and below humans."  More below

This is why AI will soon take 50%+ of sales jobs

Not because we don’t need sales.  But because AI can do a better job than this.

2. The Always-On Pressure
Humans naturally create boundaries. We go home, we sleep, we disconnect. AI agents don’t. This creates an insidious pressure to match their pace.
I caught myself checking AI-generated reports at 11 PM because “the agents found something important.” This isn’t sustainable, and it’s not what AI was supposed to solve.
